figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Planner-Aware Path Learning (PAPL) resolves training–inference mismatch in DLMs. Standard uniform training for DLMs (left) applies a uniform loss across all masked positions, distributing capacity over regions that inference-time planners never traverse. PAPL (right) introduces planner-aware weights into the loss, aligning training with the planner’s preferred trajectories (outlined arrows) and eliminating training-inference mismatch.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6: Vanilla MDM vs PAPL Training Curves. Early in training, the PAPL loss remains small because the denoiser has not yet formed meaningful beliefs about the correct token positions, causing the planner-dependent weights wi to be close to zero. As the model begins to identify correct positions with higher certainty, these weights increase, leading to a temporary rise in the PAPL loss. Once the denoiser becomes sufficiently confident, the loss decreases and eventually mirrors the behavior of the standard MDM loss. These dynamics provide additional evidence that PAPL naturally adapts its emphasis as the model’s confidence improves, stabilizing precisely when confidence becomes a reliable signal.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 defines the training–inference path mismatch; Tables 1–4 deliver protein/text/code headlines; Figures 3–4 test convergence, sampling, temperature, τ, and α; Appendix Table 5/6 isolate inference planners; Figures 5–6 and Table 7 expose instability and approximation limits.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure captions use bold title plus setup/comparison and often state the main finding. Table 1–2/4 captions define metrics and regimes; Tables 3/5–7 are shorter and rely more on body text for conditions and interpretation.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables use model/scale, sampling step, benchmark, or approximation term as top-level groups and metric as the lower-level header. Arrows, daggers, bold, and dashes encode direction, provenance, best values, and unavailable cells.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1’s planner-aware loss is evaluated in Tables 1–4, stress-tested by Figure 3/4, separated from inference planner effects in Tables 5/6, and bounded by Figures 5/6 and Table 7.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main pages carry cross-domain headline tables and the first ablation figures; Appendix B adds planner controls and Appendix C adds pure-loss failure, training dynamics, and approximation decomposition.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern typography and booktabs rules are stable across seven tables; figure captions use the same body family while raster plot labels are smaller and less inspectable.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figure 1 gray/purple paths, Figure 2 green ribbons, and Figure 3–6 curve colors are local semantic encodings rather than one global palette. Tables stay grayscale, making their structure more robust to printing than the line figures.

most_reusable_patterns: Matched state grids that make a training/inference path mismatch visible before equations.
Benchmark/metric group headers that carry multiple domains or sampling budgets without changing the scan path.
Shared-legend multi-panel curves for training, sampling, and hyperparameter interventions.
Separate inference-planner ablations from training-loss effects, followed by explicit negative diagnostics.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: defines the method interface and mismatch mechanism.
Table 1: puts protein quality, foldability thresholds, and diversity on one decision surface.
Figure 3: compactly covers convergence, sampling budget, and temperature robustness.
Figure 5 plus Table 7: expose stabilization need and the theory-to-loss approximation boundary.
failure_patterns: Most objects omit seed, interval, repetition, denominator, or task-level uncertainty.
Figures 3, 4, and 6 rely heavily on color and lose grayscale separation.
Table 3’s Oracle length condition is much stronger than ordinary PAPL and requires explicit causal reading.
Figure 5 has panel-specific apparent y scales without a caption note; Tables 5/6 can be mistaken for training effects.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper defines training–inference mismatch with one path diagram, supports PAPL with three-domain black-and-white tables, and then uses shared curves, planner controls, and appendix failure diagnostics to bound when the gains and stability claims hold.
